name: Open Books (Thoracic Rotation)
why: Improves thoracic rotation and reduces compensatory stress on the shoulder and neck during overhead movement.
instructions: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent. Reach top arm across body, then rotate open until chest faces opposite side. Repeat slowly.
dosage: 2-3 sets of 8 reps per side, daily.
contraindications: Stop if it causes sharp shoulder or rib pain.

name: Glute Bridge
why: Builds hip extension strength so the low back does less compensation under load.
instructions: Lie on back, feet flat, brace core, squeeze glutes, and lift hips to form a straight line from shoulders to knees.
dosage: 3 sets of 10-15 reps, 3-4 times per week.
contraindications: Avoid if symptoms radiate sharply down the leg.

name: Copenhagen Side Plank (Regression)
why: Targets adductor strength to improve cutting and change-of-direction tolerance.
instructions: Support top knee on bench/chair, hold side plank with lower knee bent on floor.
dosage: 3 sets of 20-30 second holds per side, 2-3 times per week.
contraindications: Modify if groin pain exceeds mild discomfort.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise Isometric
why: Isometric loading can reduce tendon pain sensitivity and rebuild force capacity.
instructions: Stand on one foot with heel elevated and hold at mid-range.
contraindications: Reduce hold time if pain escalates over the next 24 hours.

name: Split Squat Isometric
why: Provides analgesic effect and restores tolerance in the patellar tendon and quadriceps.
instructions: Hold bottom position of split squat with front knee over mid-foot.
dosage: 4-5 holds of 30-45 seconds, 3-4 times per week.
contraindications: Avoid deep range if recent ligament reconstruction without clearance.

name: Dead Bug with Breathing
why: Improves trunk control and reduces extension-based low-back irritation.
instructions: Lie on back, arms up, hips and knees at 90 degrees. Exhale while extending opposite arm/leg without arching low back.
dosage: 2-3 sets of 6-8 reps per side, 4 times per week.
contraindications: Keep range small if unable to maintain neutral spine.
